Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old male with ~1 week of non-painful swelling of the left elbow tip, assessed as likely bursitis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Noticed swelling at the tip of the left elbow about one week ago; first noticed in the shower.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began ~1 week prior; not improving; described as "weird" and slightly warm; feels like some fluid inside.
- Associated symptoms/system review: Slight warmth over the area; can move elbow normally; no systemic symptoms reported.
- Pertinent negatives: No pain or marked tenderness at the tip itself; no known local injury/trauma; no prior similar episodes; no eczema; not on regular medication; no medication allergies reported.
- Past medical history: Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
- Allergies: Allergy to peanuts (food allergy).
- Medications: Patient reports no regular medications.
- Social history / preventive care: Desk-based job; runs 2–3 times per week; otherwise mobile and active.

Examination:
- Vitals: (not documented)
- Examination findings:
  - Visual/palpation: Visible swelling at the tip/around the left elbow; area slightly warmer than adjacent skin.
  - Tip of elbow: skin dry; pressing the tip itself is tolerable; area adjacent to swelling felt "weird" by patient.
  - Range of motion: patient able to move the elbow normally.
  
Impression:
- Probable bursitis of the left elbow.
- Not clinically consistent with septic arthritis at time of assessment (septic arthritis considered unlikely presently).

Plan:
- Pharmacologic: Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if heartburn develops.
- Investigations: Arrange blood tests (full screen including inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatological antibodies, and evaluation for gout). Blood test forms to be sent to patient's home with instructions on where to attend.
- Follow-up: Review results when available (results expected ~5–6 days after testing). Follow-up appointment to be arranged; can be phone/video or face-to-face per patient preference. Patient advised to contact clinic sooner if blood test completed and review needed.
- Safety net/advice: Seek urgent assessment (phone/video or in-person) if the elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads — these findings would require immediate review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vitals (temperature, HR, BP) not documented.
  - Complete medication reconciliation and confirmation of over-the-counter or occasional medicines not documented.
  - Specific blood test names/panels and lab orders (values) not documented.
  - No imaging or aspiration performed; no culture results.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear and audible with some conversational pauses/stutters; clinically relevant details were understandable.
